terms.gloss: a man who lets himself be used sexually by men; an effeminate man; a dancer of lewd dances
evidence: Plaut. Men. 513: omnīs cinaedōs esse cēnsēs, tū quia es?
terms.comment: Greek κίναιδος. In Plautus first a dancer of wanton dances, soft and effeminate, and so a word of abuse; in Catullus and Juvenal the man who takes the passive part in sex with men. Always an insult, never a neutral word for a gay man.

terms.gloss: (of a man) who lets himself be penetrated; the passive partner
evidence: Catull. 16.2: Aurēlī pathice et cinaede Fūrī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “who submits to unnatural lust”.

phrases.latin: omnīs cinaedōs esse cēnsēs, tū quia es?
phrases.english: do you think everyone is a catamite because you are one?

phrases.latin: tum ad saltandum nōn cinaedus malacus aequest atque ego
phrases.english: and when it comes to dancing, no soft cinaedus is a match for me
